다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Think of a(n) (A)[ordinary / unique] boy who likes
playing sports like you and your friends. One day,
as he returns from school, his mom and dad are
waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His
mom smiles and says, “We have a surprise for you.”
When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is
a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He
recently joined the school’s table-tennis club and
wanted to practice (B)[less / more]. He rushes to
the other side of the net and challenges his dad to
a match.
Let’s pause the story here. The boy now faces a
big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to
grow and face difficulties with endurance and
courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging
experiences and choose an easy, (C)[familiar /
unfamiliar] path.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 여러분과 여러분의 친구들처럼 운동하는 것을 좋아하는 소년 이라 언급되었으므로, ‘ordinary(평범한)’가 알맞다. (B) 최근에 학교의 탁구 동아리에 가입한 소년은 차고에 있는 탁구대를 보고 신이 났고 또한 아빠에게 경기를 요청하므로 더 연습하고 싶어 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘more (더)’가 알맞다. (C) 인내심과 용기로 성장하고 어려움에 직면하기 위해 도전하 려는 선택과는 대조되는 내용이 와야 하므로 쉽고 익숙한 길 을 선택한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘familiar(익숙한)’가 알맞다. YBM(김은형) 1과

body:
Let’s start with the path of avoidance. The boy
waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the
ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses
it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and
sighs. “Never mind,” says his dad, “Try again.
Practice makes perfect.”
When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full
force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not
having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table,
saying, “I have had enough,” and leaves for his
room.
His dad asks for another game the next week, but
the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just
does not feel like ⓐtaking up the challenge. When
his mom suggests playing against his older brother,
he ⓑturns down her suggestion because his brother
is very tough.
“No, thanks,” sighs the boy. “He’s going to be
better than me anyway.”
In his eyes, challenges are ⓒnothing more than
obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they
are best avoided.
Let’s rewind to the point when the boy first faces
his dad across the net. His first attempt does not
go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow
on his second try. However, he picks up the ball
and tries again anyway.
An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily,
but the boy is learning from the experience. ⓓEvery
now and then, he even surprises himself with a
decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the
ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to
challenge his older brother. His brother is a better
player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work
even harder.
The boy learns from his mistakes and develops
new skills by practicing. He practices hard after
school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is
able to join the regional team. Eventually, he
ⓔparticipates in the national championship and
makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his
opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays
hard. He finds himself at match point, and the
audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he
has come. For years he has gotten up early to
practice and has loved the challenge of improving
his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the
ball past his opponent. He punches the air in
triumph. He has become truly awesome!

위 대화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 고정 사고방식을 가진 사람들이 도전을 피하는 이유이자, 실 패는 그들이 선천적으로 똑똑하지 않거나 재능이 없다는 것을 의미한다고 생각한다고 했으므로 실패에 대해 부정적 감정이 있 다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘scared(무서워하는)’가 알맞다. (B) 앞에서는 고정 사고방식을 가진 사람들이 실패를 부정적으 로 보는 견해에 대해 언급되어 있고, 괄호 다음에는 성장 사고 방식을 가진 사람들이 실패를 배울 수 있는 기회로 본다는 긍 정적인 견해가 이어지므로 대조의 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘In contrast(반면, 그와 대조적으로)’가 알맞다. (C) 성장 사고방식을 가지는 게 더 건강한 사고방식이라는 견 해에 찬성하는 답변에 이어지므로, 성장 사고방식을 갖는 것에 대한 긍정적으로 말하는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘encourages(촉진하다)’가 알맞다.

body:
Teenage life on social media might seem fun and
easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set
of challenges, both big and small. So why can
some people handle tough times and become
stronger
while
others
remain
unchanged
and
helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability
to adapt to challenging experiences, such as
(A)[expected / unexpected] events or personal
difficulties.
The good news is that humans can recover from
pressure and hardship and you can develop this
skill. However, having resilience does not mean you
will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly
normal to feel (B)[depressed / excited] every now
and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but
it will help you face and overcome them.
Think of it like building your body’s immune
system. Just as you need to be (C)[protected /
subjected] to germs to build immunity, you must
experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple
terms, resilience is not about being emotionless:
Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail.
You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like
working out to build your muscles; it takes time
and effort to enhance your resilience.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 도전이 필요한 경험의 예로 든 내용으로, 어려움이 예상되 는 사건보다는 어려움을 예상치 못한 사건이 도전적인 경험이 라는 흐름이 더 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘unexpected(예상치 못한)’ 가 알맞다. (B) 회복 탄력성이 있다는 것이 스트레스나 불안을 전혀 느끼 지 않는다는 것을 의미하지는 않는다는 내용에 이어지므로 우 울함을 느끼는 것이 지극히 정상적인 일이라는 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 따라서 ‘depressed(우울한)’가 알맞다. (C) 회복 탄력성을 키우기 위해 어려움을 경험해야 하는 것처 럼 면역력을 키우기 위해 세균에 노출되어야 하므로 세균의 영향을 받는 상태가 되어야 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘subjected(영향을 받는)’가 알맞다.

The Roman Arena
Arles is an ancient city dating back to Roman
times. Many Roman buildings remain, including an
arena that was built in 90 A.D. The arena used to
seat over 20,000 people who would go to watch
various entertaining events.
Vincent sometimes went to the bullfights that were
held in the arena every Sunday. He particularly liked
to watch the colorful crowds. He told a friend that
he found the crowds fascinating. They inspired the
painting Arena at Arles. The arena is in the top
right corner of the painting and is barely visible.
Below, there is a faint image of two bulls. However,
Vincent paid lots of attention to the people and
their colorful clothes. Some of the people are
chatting with friends, others are cheering on the
bulls, and the entire painting has a powerful energy.

Arles inspired an explosion of creativity. Vincent
claimed, “The whole future of art is to be found in
the south of France.” He worked enthusiastically and
produced nearly 200 paintings in just fifteen
months. None of Vincent’s works are left in Arles
now, but today you can see a number of them
have been recreated in street-side panels. Let’s
follow Vincent’s traces that remain in Arles.
The Roman Arena
Arles is an ancient city dating back to Roman times.
(A)서기 90년에 지어진 원형 경기장을 포함하여 많은 로마
건물들이 남아 있다. The arena used to seat over 20,000
people who would go to watch various entertaining
events.
Vincent sometimes went to the bullfights that were
held in the arena every Sunday. He particularly liked
to watch the colorful crowds. He told a friend that
he found the crowds fascinating. They inspired the
painting Arena at Arles. The arena is in the top
right corner of the painting and is barely visible.
Below, there is a faint image of two bulls. However,
Vincent paid lots of attention to the people and
their colorful clothes. Some of the people are
chatting with friends, others are cheering on the
bulls, and the entire painting has a powerful energy.
Café van Gogh
Vincent painted the world-famous Café Terrace at
Night in September 1888. He created this work
while sitting outside the Café van Gogh at night.
This was unusual because most painters did their
night scenes from memory and worked during the
daytime. As such, they used a lot of black paint.
Vincent,
however,
believed
that
night
scenes
contained diverse and vibrant colors. Indeed, the
Café Terrace at Night has such a rich harmony of
yellows, blues, and oranges that Vincent did not
have to use a single drop of black paint.
Even today, there is still a café at the site of
Vincent’s painting. It was renovated in the 1990s and
painted yellow to look like the café in the painting.
However, (B)원래 카페의 색이 노란색이었는지 아닌지
는 불확실하다. The reason is that Vincent painted
the wall of the café yellow to show the lamp light.

Former Arles Hospital
In December 1888, Vincent suffered from a mental
illness and was sent to the hospital in Arles. He
stayed there for five months. During this time, his
mental stability improved, and the doctors allowed
him to paint outdoors. Vincent took advantage of
this
freedom
and
produced
several
beautiful
landscapes, such as The Garden of the Hospital in
Arles. The picture illustrates a spring garden filled
with flowers and trees with different colors and
tones. (A)The flowers are in full bloom, and the
small trees are leafy. (B)The big trees, however,
have few leaves. (C)This is rather odd given that the
season is spring. (D)In summer, however, even the
larger trees are full of leaves and it is the ideal
season to visit Arles. (E)Perhaps this contrast reflects
the painter’s complex feelings while he was going
through the most difficult time of his life.
The hospital closed in the 1980s, and the building
reopened as a library and exhibition space, with a
café and gift shops. The garden was renovated to
resemble Vincent’s painting as much as possible.

almost entirely linear approach. The process moves in

materials for as long as possible to extract their
maximum value. Therefore, clothing and textiles are
produced, used, and reused to minimize waste. It is
a renewable approach to reduce the fashion
industry’s environmental impact.

British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment
with how (A)[easy / hard] it is to manipulate public
opinion online. He created a fake restaurant called
The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for
his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He
did not provide an exact address and wrote it was
reservations only. He did this to make people think
The Shed was an (B)[exceptional / ordinary] restaurant.
He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving
cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He
then asked his friends to write favorable fake
reviews on the review site.
ⓐThings quickly got, in Butler's words, “a little out
of hand.” From the lowest of the charts of the review
site, The Shed continuously climbed the London
rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls
requesting reservations. Interest further (C)[decreased
/ increased] when he told callers The Shed was “fully
booked for the next six weeks.”
Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The
Shed's address and sent him free samples, and
many job applications came in. These things
happened without Butler serving a single meal. The
Shed
eventually
became
London's
number-one
restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant
review sites. According to Butler, The Shed held
that ranking for two weeks.

(B) 정확한 주소에 대한 제공 없이 예약만 가능하다고 적은 이 유에 해당하므로, 그 식당이 특별한 식당이라는 이미지를 주기 위해서라는 흐름으로, ‘exceptional(특별한, 우수한)’이 알맞다. (C) 예약이 꽉 찼다고 말했을 때 식당에 대한 관심이 더욱 증 가했다는 흐름으로, ‘increased(증가했다)’가 알맞다.

Walking on the beach, you do not need to worry
about footprints. They vanish with the waves.
However, a “digital footprint” — the data trail left
when you sign up, ⓐaccess, or send content — not
only proves challenging to remove but enables
tracking of your behavior, preferences, and opinions.
There are two types of digital footprints. Active
footprints, like social media posts, are intentionally
created data, while passive footprints, such as
website ⓑcookies and mobile phone activity, occur
without your direct involvement.
 Let’s explore actions that create digital footprints.
Review the following activities and mark the ones
that you do not participate in.
Your answer should be “NONE.”
□ Creating online ⓒaccounts
□ Searching and visiting websites
□ Downloading and using apps
□ Making online purchases
□ ⓓPosting and commenting on social media
□ Sending and receiving e-mail
Your digital footprints from these activities may
remain permanent. Even if you request a website or
social media ⓔplatform to remove your personal
information, someone might have already collected
your information with bad intent. Additionally, your
negative online activity can potentially harm your
reputation or career. It is important to manage and
reduce your digital footprints.

cookie: a small file that a website stores onyour device to remember information
account: a personal profile you create on awebsite or service
post: to share something on the Internet, like apicture or a message
platform: a raised surface or structure, oftenused for people to stand on

negative online activity can potentially harm your
reputation or career. ⓕThat is important to manage

Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment
that caused little damage. However, false information
can cause emotional or financial harm to people.
For example, false information about a certain
gender or belief group can stir up hatred against
that group. It can cause fights between those who
support the group and those who do not. In
addition, misleading online reviews about questionable
products often trick people into wasting money.
To avoid being deceived by false information, we
need to develop a habit of critically evaluating what
we see online. If you see a story that looks too
good or too bad to be true, check the source first.
(A) Look at the website the story comes from. (B)
Does it look real? Are there spelling errors? Does it
have other stories or just the one you read? (C)
Click on those links and see if the other information
looks reliable. (D) Websites with false information
often do not have many real stories about other
topics. (E) They also often have lots of advertisements
that pop up when you visit the sites.

household essentials to families and individuals
transitioning from homelessness to stable housing.

in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be

do

solutions that are designed to suitably (A)meet the
specific needs of a community. Such technologies
typically utilize locally (B)available resources, so they
reduce costs and promote local industries. These
technologies are environmentally sustainable because
they rely on renewable resources. Additionally, their
designs are easy to use, ⓐ[that / which] allows

The Warka Tower is one good example of
appropriate technology. This tower (가)_______________
__________________________________________. It (C)employs
natural processes to deliver 100 liters of clean water
daily. It gathers rainwater in a pot at its base.
Additionally, the tower captures fog and ⓑ[change /
changes] it into water drops that collect on nets, and
then the water drops fall into the pot. One of the
tower’s (D)strengths is that it is simple. A small team
can construct it in just one day by using eco-friendly
materials like soil, wood, and natural fiber nets. Truly,
the Warka Tower demonstrates how appropriate
technology can (E)solve local issues in a way ⓒ[how
/ that] is affordable, effective, and eco-friendly.

body:
John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist
from the U.S. who founded Home Again in 2016. It
is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and
household essentials to families and individuals
transitioning from homelessness to stable housing.
He says, “For people who have lived in their cars,
in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be
home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and
something to be celebrated.”
John’s journey began in 2015. At the age of
twelve, he volunteered at a local shelter where
people in need were staying. He learned that many
of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses
and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their
new homes upon moving in. This prompted John to
decide to do something for those transitioning out
of homelessness. Needing donations to gather
essential items to help them, John reached out to
his family, friends, and neighbors. As word of his
efforts spread, donations began to rush in. So John
was able to help more people get settled. He said,
“I never knew the impact that a simple couch or a
kitchen table could have. Furniture can restore the
dignity of a family.”

specific needs of a community. Such technologies

reduce costs and promote local industries. These

appropriate technology. This tower helps with the

daily. It gathers rainwater in a pot at its base.

a

that

In 1768, Hwang Yun-seok, a scholar, made a diary
entry after taking the gwageo, a public service
entrance exam. He wrote (A)[what / that] he and
his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon
for lunch. Hwang’s diary is the first historical
ⓐdocument indicating Koreans have been delivering
food for at least two and a half centuries.
During the Joseon period, ⓑspecialized people called
jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before
the modern address systems, letters were delivered
by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to
know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service
prices were determined by schedule and distance.
During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul’s streets
were filled with delivery professionals called “messengers,”
most working for a company (B)[was named / named]
Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery.
When customers ⓒcontacted Yongdalsa, a messenger
went to pick up the item and then delivered it.
Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes
ⓓcharged with carrying large bundles of cash, but
they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers
trusted the messengers so much that they often did
not check the items they (C)[were received /
received]. This messenger service was unique to
Korea and was based on a culture of ⓔmutual
trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this
paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery.

After Korea’s liberation from colonial rule, it was
divided into two. Then came the Korean War
(1950-1953). During this series of upheavals, Korea’s
delivery system (A)[collapsed / stabilized]. It was
during the 1960s that delivery services grew again
thanks to urbanization. As economic development
progressed, people flocked to urban areas, where
labor
became
concentrated.
This
boosted
the
demand
for
delivery
services.
Deliveries
of
newspapers and milk quickly became (B)[unpopular
/ popular]. During lunchtime, city centers were filled
with restaurant workers delivering trays full of food,
stacked on top of each other. In the late 1980s and
1990s, caterers delivered homemade lunches in
cloth bags to urban offices and returned later to
collect empty dishes. The delivery area grew rapidly.
In 1992, taekbae service, an express home delivery
service through which a person receives an ordered
item in at least a day or two, was introduced. On
the first day, there were just two deliveries. Now,
millions of items are delivered daily. On average, a
South Korean uses taekbae sixty-five times per year.
It was the development of digital and information
technology
that
(C)[impeded
/
allowed]
the
remarkable growth of taekbae. Logistics automation,
GPS maps, and mobile applications have extended
the range and scale of delivery services while
keeping prices reasonable. The phenomenal growth
of e-commerce has driven the need for delivery
services.
A rule of thumb for taekbae is next-day delivery; if
a person orders something today, it should arrive
tomorrow. Taekbae is changing so rapidly that now
more and more items are delivered on the same
day they are ordered. It is also possible to choose
a specific date and time for delivery.

This service is carried out by dedicated people

The delivery process begins early in the morning

deliveries. Dabbawalas have a simple but effective
color-coding system to ensure each lunch box
reaches its planned destination. Dabbawalas owe
their success to an efficient organization and a
strong sense of work. Accuracy is key, and their
cooperation and communication allow them to
function as efficiently as a well-organized machine.

After Korea’s liberation from colonial rule, it was
divided into two. Then came the Korean War
(1950-1953). During this series of upheavals, Korea’s
delivery system (A)[collapsed / stabilized]. It was
during the 1960s that delivery services grew again
thanks to urbanization. As economic development
progressed, people flocked to urban areas, where
labor
became
concentrated.
This
boosted
the
demand
for
delivery
services.
Deliveries
of
newspapers and milk quickly became (B)[unpopular
/ popular]. During lunchtime, city centers were filled
with restaurant workers delivering trays full of food,
stacked on top of each other. In the late 1980s and
1990s, caterers delivered homemade lunches in
cloth bags to urban offices and returned later to
collect empty dishes. The delivery area grew rapidly.
In 1992, taekbae service, an express home delivery
service through which a person receives an ordered
item in at least a day or two, was introduced. On
the first day, there were just two deliveries. Now,
millions of items are delivered daily. On average, a
South Korean uses taekbae sixty-five times per year.
It was the development of digital and information
technology
that

/
allowed]
the
remarkable growth of taekbae. Logistics automation,
GPS maps, and mobile applications have extended
the range and scale of delivery services while
keeping prices reasonable. The phenomenal growth
of e-commerce has driven the need for delivery
services.
A rule of thumb for taekbae is next-day delivery; if
a person orders something today, it should arrive
tomorrow. Taekbae is changing so rapidly that now
more and more items are delivered on the same
day they are ordered. It is also possible to choose
a specific date and time for delivery.

and

solution: ⓐ 포용적인 언어는 다양성을 인정하고, 차이에 대한 민감성을 장려하며, 평등한 기회를 촉진하는 중요한 역할을 한다고 했으 므로, 편견과 차별적인 언어를 없애는 데 적극적으로 기여한다 는 흐름으로 ‘eliminating(제거하는 것)’이 알맞다. ⓑ '맹인' 대신 '시각 장애를 가진 사람'을 선택하는 것의 효과로, 뒤에 각 개인의 고유한 정체성과 존엄성을 강조한다는 내용과 함께 제시되어 있으므로, 사람을 특수한 하나의 특성으로 축소 시키는 것을 피한다는 흐름으로 ‘preventing(막는)’이 알맞다. ⓒ 포용적인 언어는 다양성을 인정하고, 평등한 기회를 촉진하 는 중요한 도구 역할을 하며, 성이나 특성 보다 사람을 우선시 한다고 했으므로, 포용적 언어는 공정하고 따뜻한 사회를 만드 는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 흐름으로 ‘impartial(공정한)’이 알 맞다.

In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering
American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the
Earth for the first time in American history. NASA
used an electronic computer, first introduced into
the space program a year earlier, to calculate the
spaceship’s trajectory, but it made many minor
errors.
Glenn,
who

concerned
about
its
accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check
the machine’s figures by hand. “If she says the
numbers are good,” he said, “I’m good to go.”
Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine
spent a day and a half checking the calculations
and finally (B)[disproved / made sure of] them.
Eventually,
Glenn
became
the
first
American
astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part
of the team that performed calculations for Apollo
11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in
1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars,
which is still being worked on today.
Katherine retired in 1986 after thirty-three years at
NASA. After that, she dedicated the rest of her life
to championing access to *STEM education for
Black girls. For her contributions, President Barack
Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of
Freedom in 2015 and said, “Katherine G. Johnson
refused to be limited by society’s expectations of
her gender and race while (C)[expanding / reducing]
the boundaries of humanity’s reach.” In 2017, NASA
dedicated a building in her honor in Virginia and
named it the Katherine G. Johnson Computational
Research Facility. She died on February 24, 2020, at
the age of 101, but her pioneering legacy will never
be forgotten.

solution: (A) 미국의 선구적인 우주 비행사인 존 글렌은 우주선의 궤적 을 계산하기 위해 NASA에 의해 처음 도입된 전자 컴퓨터의 정확도를 걱정해서 캐서린 존슨에게 기계의 수치를 수동으로 다시 확인해 달라고 요청했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 캐서린의 놀라운 수동 계산은 디지털 컴퓨터보다 더 신뢰를 받았다는 흐름으로 ‘trusted(신뢰를 받는)’가 알맞다. Klara is an AF (Artificial Friend), a companion robot
for children. She is solar-powered. She stays healthy
when she gets the Sun’s nourishment but feels
weak and lifeless without sunlight. At the robot
store, she enjoyed taking in the outside world from
the windows. (A)클라라는 배려하고 도움이 되는 AF가
되기 위해서 필요한 모든 것을 배우기를 희망하면서,
자신이 본 것을 면밀히 관찰했다. One evening, she
discovered that a homeless man was lying on the
street without moving. Klara was sad as she
believed he had died. But the next morning when

the homeless man was sitting up and stroking his
dog. Klara believed the Sun had saved him and
came to have strong faith in the Sun’s power to
restore everything.

just creating a digital base map; it played a crucial

and technology to address local issues and promote

urban convenience and of providing invaluable
assistance in disaster response efforts.

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
solution: ⓐ 뒤에 다른 동사가 없으므로 주어 volunteers and organizers에 이어 지는 동사 자리로, 흐름상 과거의 일을 설명하고 있으므로 과거형 동 사 employed가 알맞다. 참고로 from the OpenStreetMap community는 주어를 수식하는 전치사구이며, quickly는 동사를 수식하는 부사이다. ⓑ 등위접속사 and에 의해, 앞의 명사구 community mapping을 수식 하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to save의 동사원형 save와 병렬 연 결되고 있으므로, 동사원형인 make가 알맞다. ⓒ 선행사 a community-driven process를 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사 뒤의 동사는 선행사에 수일치 시 키므로 선행사인 단수명사구 a community-driven process에 수일치시킨 단수동사 utilizes가 알맞다.

volunteers and organizers from the OpenStreetMap
community quickly employed satellite images to

따라서 답은 ②이다.

to

small-mouthed
frogs
called

woods.

sad reality that puts these little frogs at risk. During
a TV interview, Paul expressed (C)[hope / concern]
that if nothing is done soon, the situation will
repeat itself.
Fortunately, the government has made a plan to

nature. It is time for humans to take action and

Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, “I counted everything—the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed.” She excitedly added, “I couldn’t wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry.” But Katherine’s hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so
ⓐ _____ she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses ⓑ _____ the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. “You would make a good research mathematician,” he told his seventeen-year-old student, “and I’m going to prepare you for this career.” Katherine asked, “ⓒ _____ will I find a job?” “That,” he replied, “will be your problem.” The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew ⓓ _____ she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At ⓔ time, teaching was the only option available to her.

(A) Why did Katherine's father move the family 200 kilometers away?
(B) Why was Katherine's mentor not happy when telling her about career opportunities?
(C) Why did Katherine begin her career as a teacher?
answer: (A) It is because her hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. (B) It is because he had to tell his outstanding student about her limited career opportunities. (C) It is because at that time, teaching was the only option available to her as a black woman.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Inclusive Language Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities.
(A) It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a welcoming environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term “mail carrier” instead of “mailman” or “mailwoman” conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. (B) This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender.
(C) Many ancient languages disappeared because younger generations stopped using them. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying “colored people,” we should use “people of color.” Similarly, opting for “person with blindness” over “blind person” highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic.
(D) In summary, inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair and welcoming society, where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self without the fear of exclusion. (E) Such language choices can positively influence the way people understand and respect one another.

다음 글을 읽고, inclusive communication의 또 다른 측면으로 언급된 표현을 본문에서 찾아 두 단어 이내로 쓰시오.
→ 1회차 실전 모의고사
solution: 본문에서는 inclusive communication의 또 다른 측면으로 person-first language를 제시하고 있다. 이는 사람의 특정 특징보다 개인 자체를 우선적으로 존중하는 표현 방식을 의미한다.

Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything─the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry." But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" ⓐ"That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her. 실전 모의고사 2회차

choices: The mentor knew that the specific job she wanted was already filled.
The mentor refused to help her find a job because she was still a student.
The mentor believed that finding a job was the final test of her capabilities.
The mentor was concerned that her talent alone could not erase social hurdles.
The mentor was confident that she could solve the problem of finding a job, just as she solved math problems.
solution: Katherine Johnson의 어린 시절 천재성과 사회적 인종 차별 속에서도 굴하지 않고 자신의 길을 개척해 나갔다는 내용의 글이다. 이처럼 당시 흑인 여성이 연구직으로 취업하기 힘든 사회적 장애물을 그녀 스스로 헤쳐 나가야 함을 의미하므로, 추론할 수 있는 내용은 ④ '멘토는 그녀의 재능만으로 사회적 장벽을 지울 수 없다고 걱정했다.'이다.

This specific mastery of manual computation earned her a unique professional title among her peers and supervisors. Katherine Johnson's role at NASA involved critical tasks such as calculating trajectories, ideal launch timing, and emergency return paths for early space exploration efforts, including the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969. (A) Her mathematical precision was so reliable that it was considered essential not only for the moon landing but also for the beginning of the Space Shuttle program and future plans for a mission to Mars. (B) She manually performed these complex tasks in an era when electronic computers were often prone to error or entirely unavailable. (C) She was known as a "human computer" for her tremendous mathematical capability and ability to work with space trajectories. (D) It is truly remarkable that she achieved such precision with such little technology available to her. (E) Furthermore, she accomplished this with very little public recognition at the time, working quietly behind the scenes of history.
solution: Katherine Johnson이 NASA에서 수행한 수학적 계산의 중요성과 정확성을 설명하는 내용의 글이다. 주어진 문장은 이러한 수동 계산의 구체적인 숙달은 동료와 상사들 사이에서 그녀에게 독특한 직업적 칭호를 안겨주었다는 내용이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 그녀가 수동으로 계산을 수행했다는 문장이 있어야 하고, 뒤에는 칭호에 대한 문장이 이어져야 한다. (C) 앞에서 수동 계산을 언급하고, (C) 뒤에서 인간 컴퓨터는 칭호를 밝히므로, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은 ③ (C)이다.

밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 틀린 것은?
Inclusive Language Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities. It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a welcoming environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term “mail carrier” instead of “mailman” or “mailwoman” conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying “colored people,” we should use “people of color.” Similarly, opting for “person with blindness” over “blind person” highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. In summary, inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair and welcoming society, where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self without the fear of exclusion.
choices: inclusivity : the practice of including people of different backgrounds and identities equally
gender-neutral : showing preference toward one particular gender
prioritize : to treat something as more important than other things
embrace : to accept something willingly and positively
solution: ① inclusivity는 ‘포용성’이라는 뜻으로, 다양한 배경을 가진 사람들을 동등하게 포함하는 태도를 의미하므로 올바른 설명이다. ② gender-neutral은 ‘특정 성별에 치우치지 않는, 성 중립적인’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문에서는 “한 특정 성별을 선호하는”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. ③ prioritize는 ‘우선시하다’라는 뜻으로 적절하다. ④ crucial은 ‘매우 중요한’이라는 의미로 문맥에 맞다. ⑤ embrace는 ‘기꺼이 받아들이다’라는 뜻으로 올바른 설명이다.

밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 맞는 것은?
Katherine Johnson, a "Computer" Who Looked Beyond Numbers Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, “I counted everything—the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed.” She excitedly added, “I couldn’t wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry.” But Katherine’s hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. “You would make a good research mathematician,” he told his seventeen-year-old student, “and I’m going to prepare you for this career.” Katherine asked, “Where will I find a job?” “That,” he replied, “will be your problem.” The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way.
choices: prodigy : a young person who has an unusually great ability in something
algebra : a subject that studies living things and the natural environment
geometry : the study of past events and human societies
segregate : to encourage different groups of people to work together equally
obstacle : a reward or benefit given for excellent performance
solution: ① prodigy는 “특정 분야에서 뛰어난 재능을 가진 천재적인 아이(young person with exceptional talent)”라는 뜻으로, 제시된 영영 풀이가 알맞다. 본문에서도 Katherine Johnson이 어린 시절부터 뛰어난 수학 능력을 보였다고 설명한다. ② algebra는 ‘대수학’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “생물과 자연환경을 연구하는 학문”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. 이는 biology에 가까운 설명이다. ③ geometry는 ‘기하학’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “과거 사건과 인간 사회를 연구하는 학문”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. 이는 history의 설명에 해당한다. ④ segregate는 ‘분리하다, 차별하여 구분하다’라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “서로 다른 집단이 평등하게 함께 일하도록 장려하다”라고 설명하고 있으므로 반대 의미이다. ⑤ obstacle은 ‘장애물, 방해물’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문은 “훌륭한 성과에 대해 주어지는 보상”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. 이는 reward와 유사한 의미이다.

Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything – the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry." But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school.
(A) So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. (B) After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. (C) Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. (D) "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." (E) The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her.

윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적 절한 곳은?
By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer.
solution: Katherine이 가진 능력에도 불구하고 겪었던 차별을 설명하는 내용의 글이다. 주어진 문장은 3학년 때까지 그녀는 대학이 제공할 수 있는 모든 수학 과정을 이수했다는 내용이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 대학 입학 직후의 상황에 대한 문장이 있어야 하고, 뒤에는 더 이상 들을 수업이 없어 멘토가 특별 수업을 제공하게 된 문장이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은 ③ (C) 이다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities. It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a (A) environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term “mail carrier” instead of “mailman” or “mailwoman” conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, ⓐencourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying “colored people,” we should use “people of color.” Similarly, opting for “person with blindness” over “blind person” highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. In summary, inclusive language plays a crucial role in creating a fair and (B) _____ society, (C) [where / her / embrace / self / every / without / of / can / genuine / exclusion / or / the / his / individual / fear].

(C)에 주어진 단어들을 <보기>의 해석에 맞게 바르게 재배 열하시오.
보기 모든 개인이 배제될 두려움 없이 자신의 진정한 모 습을 드러낼 수 있는
→
answer: where every individual can embrace his or her genuine self without the fear of exclusion

solution: ② 제시된 풀이 'to give out things to each person in a group(그룹의 각 사람에게 물건을 나눠주다)'는 count(세다) 의 뜻과 전혀 다른 개념이다. count의 올바른 풀이는 'to say or find the total number of things in a group(그룹 안의 사물의 총 수를 말하거나 구하다)'이다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ① youngest(막내, 가장 어린): 어떤 집단에서 가장 최근에 태어난 사람 ③ wash(씻다): 물과 비누를 사용하여 무언가를 깨끗이 하다 ④ add(덧붙이다): 이미 말해진 것에 무언가를 더 말하다 ⑤ wait(기다리다): 특정한 일이 일어날 때까지 어딘가에 머물다

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Katherine Johnson was born on August 26, 1918, in West Virginia, in the U.S., and was the youngest of four children in a black family. Katherine was a math prodigy from early childhood. Reflecting on her youth, Katherine once said, "I counted everything-the steps to the road, the steps up to church, the number of dishes, spoons, and forks I washed." She excitedly added, "I couldn't wait to get to high school to take algebra and geometry.“ But Katherine's hometown had a segregated education system, and black students could not enter high school. So her father moved the family 200 kilometers away so that she could enter high school. After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles, but Katherine knew she had the strength to make her own way. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her.

윗글의 Katherine이 그녀의 멘토와의 대화 이후 느꼈을 감정으로 가장 적절한 것은?
solution: 앞길이 불투명하고 장애물이 가득했지만, Katherine은 자신만의 길을 개척할 힘이 있다는 것을 알았으므로, 그녀의 감정은 ② determined(단호한)이다.

choices: Katherine Johnson은 어린 시절부터 문학과 역사에 특 별한 관심을 보였다.

다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
After graduating from high school in 1932, she was admitted to a black college at the age of fifteen. By her junior year, she had taken all the math courses the college could offer. Her mentor gladly offered special classes just for her, but he was not happy when he had to tell his outstanding student about her career opportunities. "You would make a good research mathematician," he told his seventeen-year-old student, "and I'm going to prepare you for this career." Katherine asked, "Where will I find a job?" "That," he replied, "will be your problem." The path ahead was unclear and full of obstacles due to her gender and race. In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option available to her. Despite being a math prodigy who graduated with highest honors, Katherine began her career as a teacher because _____ .
choices: she preferred teaching mathematics to young black students over research
she was too young to enter the competitive field of research and engineering
her mentor advised her that teaching was the best way to prepare for stable career
she wanted to use the salary from teaching to finance her graduate studies later
social barriers based on her race and gender limited her professional options to the teaching field
solution: Katherine이 실력을 갖췄지만, 당대의 현실로 어려움을 겪는 내용으로, 그녀가 교사가 된 이유로 당시의 인종 및 성별 장벽이 직업적 선택지를 제한했다는 내용이 와야 할 것이다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤ '그녀의 인종과 성별에 기반한 사회적 장벽이 그녀의 직업적 선택을 교육 분야로 제한했다’이다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Katherine의 성격을 묘사한 것으로 가 장 적절한 것은?
Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA's elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Regardless of her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that "the girls" didn't usually go. Katherine asked, "Is there a law that says I can't go?" The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with confidence. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division received credit as an author of a research report.
solution: Katherine은 차별적 규정에 굴하지 않고 당당하게 권리를 쟁취했으므로, 성격으로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤ '용기 있고 자신감 넘치는'이다.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go." Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations and finally made sure of them. Eventually, Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part of the team that performed calculations for Apollo 11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in 1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today.

NASA used a new electronic computer to calculate the spaceship's path, but it made a few big mistakes.
Glenn told Katherine Johnson to confirm the machine's numbers by hand.
Katherine also worked on the team that calculated for Apollo 11.
The plan to send astronauts for Mars, which is still in progress, is being worked on.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
It was not until 1953 that Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the "Black computers" who did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and being referred to with terms like "girl" despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA's elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Despite her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that "the girls" didn't usually go. Katherine asked, "Is there a law that says I can't go?" The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with courage. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division received credit as an author of a research report. Katherine's remarkable calculations by hand were trusted more than digital computers. In early 1962, John Glenn, one of the pioneering American astronauts, was preparing to orbit the Earth for the first time in American history. NASA used an electronic computer, first introduced into the space program a year earlier, to calculate the spaceship's trajectory, but it made many minor errors. Glenn, who was concerned about its accuracy, asked Katherine Johnson to double-check the machine's figures by hand. "If she says the numbers are good," he said, "I'm good to go." Using only a pencil and a slide rule, Katherine spent a day and a half checking the calculations and finally made sure of them. Eventually, Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth. Katherine was also part of the team that performed calculations for Apollo 11, which sent the first three men to the Moon in 1969, and even the plan to put people on Mars, which is still being worked on today. Katherine retired in 1986 after thirty-three years at NASA. After that, she dedicated the rest of her life to championing access to STEM education for Black girls. For her contributions, President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015 and said, "Katherine G. Johnson refused to be limited by society's expectations of her gender and race while expanding the boundaries of humanity's reach." In 2017, NASA dedicated a building in her honor in Virginia and named it the Katherine G. Johnson Computational Research Facility. She died on February 24, 2020, at the age of 101, but her pioneering legacy will never be forgotten.

Language has the power to shape our attitudes and behaviors. Inclusive language serves as an important tool for acknowledging diversity, encouraging sensitivity to differences, and promoting equal opportunities. It actively contributes to breaking biases and discriminatory language and to building a welcoming environment of inclusivity. For example, adopting the gender-neutral term "mail carrier" instead of "mailman" or "mailwoman" conveys a powerful message: it recognizes the capabilities of individuals of either gender for delivering the mail. This seemingly minor change reflects a more extensive commitment to acknowledging the ability of every person, regardless of his or her gender. Another aspect of inclusive communication, known as person-first language, encourages us to prioritize the individual over any defining characteristic. Instead of saying "colored people," we should use "people of color." Similarly, opting for "person with blindness" over "blind person" highlights the unique identity and dignity of each individual while avoiding the reduction of a person to an unusual characteristic. Inclusive language is a vital tool that actively shapes perceptions by acknowledging (A) and breaking down discriminatory biases. It operates through specific strategies, such as using gender-neutral terms to focus on capability, and employing person-first language to (B) _____ the individual over their defining characteristics. Ultimately, the goal of this linguistic shift is to foster a more (C) and welcoming society where everyone feels respected and free from the fear of exclusion.

body:

The Amazon rainforest is often referred to as the "lungs of the planet" because of its role in absorbing carbon dioxide. It produces 20% of the world's oxygen, ⓐthat explains why protecting it is crucial for global climate stability. The ecosystem, ⓑin which millions of species of insects and plants coexist, is currently under threat. We must implement policies ⓒthat can effectively prevent illegal logging.
→
solution: ⓐ: 앞의 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 써야 한다. (that은 계속적 용법으로 쓸 수 없다.)

body:

My sister worked very intense schedules as a teacher and relaxed only on vacations. When I was little, she constantly pushed me to finish my assignments, (A)[that / which] I despised. Indeed, she was a trustworthy person dealing with an untrustworthy kid. For instance, one afternoon she told me to paint the fence and I chose (B)
[painting / to paint] just the back section. But it was windy for some days and the front section became so weathered (C)[that / while] I had to prepare it with primer first. By the time I completed it, the back section was too faded to paint properly, and so forth. *primer: 밑칠용 페인트
solution: (A) 앞에 나온 절 전체를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사는 'which'이다. (B) 'choose'는 목적어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이다. (C) 문맥상 원인과 결과를 나타내는 부사절 접속사 'so + 형용사/부사 + that'이 필요하다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장을 고르시오.
choices: Reach out to the newcomers, that are struggling to adapt.
The only solution that I can think of is patience.
What surprised me most was how calm she remained.
This program is designed for whoever wants to improve their skills.
They stayed at a charming inn, the owner of which was very friendly.
solution: ①은 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 that을 쓸 수 없으므로 틀리다. that을 who로 고쳐야 한다. ②는 the only solution을 선행사로 하는 제한적 용법의 that으로 올바르다. ③은 선행사가 없는 관계대명사 what으로 올바르다. ④는 whoever가 명사절을 이끌어 전치사 for의 목적어 역할을 하므로 올바르다. ⑤는 'the owner of which' 구조로 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
The platypus is one of the most unusual mammals in the world. Its name was derived from the Greek words platus and pous, (A)[that / which] mean "flat foot," referring to its webbed feet. The platypus can detect electrical signals from prey underwater, (B)[although / despite] it doesn't have very good eyesight. Platypuses belong to a group of mammals called monotremes, and that name refers to mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young. To put it more concretely, they are egg-laying mammals (C)[like / alike] echidnas. Also, they belong to the family Ornithorhynchidae. Other than platypuses, there are no other living members of that family. *monotreme 단공류 **Ornithorhynchidae 오리너구리과
solution: (A) 콤마 뒤에서 앞의 명사(the Greek words platus and pous)를 계속적으로 설명하는 관계대명사 자리이므로 that이 아닌 which가 와야 한다. (B) 뒤에 '주어+동사'로 이루어진 절(it doesn't have very good eyesight)이 이어지므로 접속사 although가 필요하다. despite는 전치사로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 한다. (C) 뒤에 명사(echidnas)가 이어지므로 전치사 like가 적절하다. alike는 명사를 수식하는 자리에 쓰일 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 ① which - although - like이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:

Why Does My Face Turn Red? It has nothing to do with you being ashamed. It’s your blood vessels that are to blame! Vessels are like flexible tubes that carry blood throughout your body. Feeling nervous or embarrassed expands the vessels, ⓐ(the skin, makes, which, red). The brain sends a signal to increase blood flow, so the temperature of your face rises and you feel hot. If you want to keep yourself aware of your physical reactions, pay attention to how your body responds to stress.
→
solution: 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which 뒤에 '동사(makes) + 목적어(the skin) + 형용사 보어(red)' 구문을 연결한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Creativity often begins with ordinary curiosity,
ⓐthat you nurture through constant questioning and exploration. This is true of simple curiosity, such as ⓑwhy the sky changes color at sunset. You don't discover a truly original idea ⓒuntil you connect unrelated pieces of information in a new way. Such connections are strengthened once they ⓓare tested repeatedly against real-world problems, becoming more reliable over time. When ideas finally take shape, they reveal insights, which are remarkably ⓔsurprising, as well as questions you hadn't considered. *curiosity 호기심 *nurture 기르다, 육성하다
solution: ⓐ 콤마 뒤에서 계속적 용법으로 쓰이는 관계대명사에는 that을 쓸 수 없으므로 that을 which로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ why the sky changes color at sunset은 ‘왜 해 질 녘에 하늘의 색이 변하는지’라는 의미의 명사절로 such as 뒤에 적절하게 쓰였다. ⓒ don't ~ until은 ‘~할 때까지 …하지 않다’라는 의미를 나타내므로 적절하다. ⓓ once they are tested에서 connections는 시험되는 대상이므로 수동태 are tested가 적절하다. ⓔ surprising은 which가 가리키는 insights의 성질을 설명하는 형용사로, be동사 are 뒤의 보어로 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

In 1935, at the age of eighteen, Katherine graduated from college with highest honors and began her career as a teacher at a black public school. At that time, teaching was the only option
ⓐavailable to her. It was not until 1953 that Katherine found a job at a NASA field center in Virginia. There, she worked as one of the “Black computers” who ⓑ did complex calculations manually to support white male engineers. Though they greatly contributed to the space project, they endured a lot of discrimination, including segregation in the office and ⓒbeing referred to with terms like “girl” despite being professional women. Two weeks into the job, Katherine was reassigned to NASA’s elite space research division. There, she was the only black female member of the staff. Despite her enormous contributions, the important research meetings were held only among white staff members. When she asked for permission to attend the meetings, her male colleagues said that “the girls” didn’t usually go. Katherine asked, “Is there a law that ⓓsay I can’t go?” The embarrassed male workers had no choice but to let her in. By asking questions no one had ever asked, Katherine ended a discriminatory custom. She had faced barriers, but her efforts to overcome them paid off. She felt proud and continued her work with courage. In 1960, she wrote a research paper with another engineer about how to place a spacecraft into orbit. That was the first time a woman in her division ⓔreceived credit as an author of a research report. 실전 학습

<보기>의 관점에서 윗글의 Klara에 대해 보일 반응으로 적절하지 않은 것은?

choices: 필요했다면 인간을 대체할 수도 있었다고 말하는 것은 인간 의 필요를 충족시키려는 기계의 근본적 목적을 지키기 위해 서야.
Josie를 잇는 일이 잘 안 되었을 것이라고 성공 가능성을 성 급히 평가하기보다, 원래의 임무를 수행하는 행위 자체에 더 집중해야 해.
한계 너머에 무엇인가가 항상 남아있을 것이라는 말은 임무 의 실현 가능성을 현실적인 측면으로 제시하는 모습이야.

윗글의 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 적절한 문장의 개수는?
solution: ⓒ 조건문 내에서 과거 사실과 반대되는 일을 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 구문이다. ⓔ 접속사 that이 이끄는 명사절이 보어로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓕ 조동사의 과거형 뒤에 완료형을 써서 과거에 대한 강한 추측을 나타낸다. ⓐ a place를 수식하는 표현 뒤에 절이 갖추어져 있으므로, which는 where로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ do의 목적어 역할을 수행하면서 삽입절의 주어를 이끄는 관계대명사가 와야 하므로, that은 what으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ 가정법 과거완료 시제가 등위접속사 but과 동일하게 이어져 있으므로, remain은 have remained로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 어법상 적절한 문장의 개수는 3개이다.

In Josie’s country home, Klara found out that Josie had gone through a procedure known as “lifting.” By being lifted, Josie’s cognitive abilities had been genetically ⓐ enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities. However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of her sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end. Because of this, Josie spent most of her time at home and was being educated there.
(A) To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie suspended in the air—it was an AF replica of Josie’s body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara’s consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to ⓑsurvive.
(B) One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi’s studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after ⓒcompleting the questionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi’s office.
(C) Capaldi: Klara, tell me what you think about the replica.
Klara: It ⓓresembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of capturing Josie’s appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to ⓔobserve and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her _____ and feelings.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Josie became healthier after the lifting procedure without any side effects.
Mr. Capaldi was actually a scientist rather than a painter.
Klara refused to answer questions about Josie in the studio.
Josie attended school regularly outside her home.
Chrissie wanted to stop Klara from learning about Josie.
solution: 본문에서 Mr. Capaldi는 화가가 아니라 과학자이며, Klara의 의식을 replica에 옮겨 새로운 Josie를 만들 계획을 세우고 있었다고 설명된다. 따라서 ②가 옳다. ① Josie는 lifting 이후 심각한 부작용과 만성 질환에 시달렸다. ③ Klara는 Josie에 대한 questionnaire에 답했다. ④ Josie는 대부분 집에서 교육을 받았다. ⑤ Chrissie는 오히려 Klara에게 Josie를 계속 관찰하고 배우도록 요청했다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Klara의 깨달음으로 가장 적절한 것은?
After several rainy days, the Sun came out to shine light on Josie and her whole bed. Josie woke up and made a miraculous recovery. Seasons and years went by, and she grew into a healthy adult. When Josie left for college, Klara was sent to the Yard, a place where old AFs spend their remaining days at the end of their lives. In the Yard, she remembered her days with Josie.
Klara: Josie was the best teenager for me. I did all I could to learn Josie and to do what was best for her. If it had become necessary, I could have continued Josie. But I don’t think it would have worked out so well. Not because I wouldn’t have achieved accuracy, but however hard I tried, I believe now there would have remained something beyond my reach. Mr. Capaldi believed there was nothing special inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But it wasn’t inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. I would have never reached what they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.
choices: 기술이 발전하면 로봇도 인간의 감정을 완벽히 지닐 수 있 다.
인간을 특별하게 만드는 것은 인간 그 자체가 아니라 타인 을 향한 사랑이다.
아픈 환자를 회복시키는 데에는 태양빛보다 의학 치료가 훨 씬 중요하다.
AF는 수명이 다하면 Yard에서 새로운 임무를 부여받는다.
완벽한 정확성만 갖추면 누군가의 삶을 완벽히 대체할 수 있다.
solution: 클라라는 카팔디 씨(Mr. Capaldi)의 생각과 달리 조시에게 아주 특별한 무언가가 존재했지만, 그것은 조시 개인의 내면이 아니라 '조시를 사랑했던 사람들의 마음속'에 있었다고 말한다. 즉, 인간을 진정 특별하게 만드는 핵심 요소는 개인 그 자체의 물리적·기계적 특성이 아니라 타인을 향한 사랑과 감정이라는 것을 깨닫게 된다. 따라서 ②가 정답이다. ① 클라라는 아무리 노력해도 사람들의 마음속 감정에 다다를 수 없었을 것이라 고백하므로 글의 내용과 반대된다. ③ 지문에서 태양빛에 의해 조시가 기적적으로 회복된 장면은 나오지만, 의학 치료와의 비교는 언급되지 않았다. ④ Yard는 새로운 임무를 받는 곳이 아니라 오래된 AF들이 삶의 마지막 날들을 보내는 장소이다. ⑤ 클라라는 정확성을 갖추었더라도 타인의 마음속 깊은 사랑까지 대체할 수는 없었을 것이라고 밝히고 있다.

다음 글에서 Capaldi가 'Klara가 Josie의 욕구와 열망을 이해하는 과정에 잘 도달해 있다'는 증거로 제시한 것을 본 문에서 찾아 2단어로 쓰시오.
Capaldi: Klara, tell me what you think about the replica.
Klara: It resembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of capturing Josie’s appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to observe and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her decisions and feelings.
Capaldi: We will ask you to become her and to live in that replica of Josie with everything you have learned. Learn Josie, not just superficially, but deeply, entirely. You have to continue her for Chrissie and for everyone else who loves Josie.
Chrissie: I have doubts. I’m still not sure if this whole plan is the best thing we can do. I have been afraid of losing Josie ever since I lost Sal. That is why I agreed with you on this replica, but however well you make it, I don’t think I will be able to accept this AF as my Josie.
Capaldi: You must not lose faith, Chrissie. The survey Klara has successfully completed is clear evidence that she is already well on her way to understanding all of Josie’s drives and desires. You believe that there is something unreachable inside each of us, something that is unique and won’t transfer. But there is nothing like that. The new Josie won’t be an imitation. She will be the exact same person and you will have every right to love her just as you love Josie now.
Chrissie: But will I believe in it? When the day comes, will I really?
Klara: Excuse me, but I would like to say there 06 is a chance you will never need the new Josie. She may overcome her illness. If wrong to give up hope already.
→
solution: 본문에서 Capaldi가 Chrissie를 설득하는 대화 부분에서 'Klara가 성공적으로 작성 마친 그 설문지(The survey)는 그녀가 이미 Josie의 모든 욕구와 열망을 이해하는 과정에 잘 도달해 있다는 명확한 증거이다'라고 했으므로 Capaldi가 증거로 직접 제시한 핵심 대상은 Klara가 완료한 설문지(The survey)이다.

Klara: (nodding hopefully)
Josie: That’s so good, but I want to be honest with you. I know how bad you’ll feel after people promise you perfect things and they turn out not to be so. Some days I’m not so healthy or happy. I do not know why. Do you still want to come, Klara?

answer: (1) 긍정적 결과: 유전자 조작을 통해 인지 능력이 향상되어 명 문 대학에 진학할 수 있는 더 좋은 기회를 갖게 되었다. (2) 부정적 결과: 심각한 부작용과 원인을 알 수 없는 만성 질 환에 시달려 며칠씩 누워 지내야 했고, 집에서 교육을 받아야 했다.

The CRISPR Gene-Editing Tool Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. It is important to ensure that gene editing’s potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.
choices: demonstrate : to hide something from other people
incurable : impossible to cure or heal
ethical : causing harm or unfair treatment to others
comprehensive : very short and lacking important details
innovative : old-fashioned and unwilling to change 유형보충독해
solution: ② incurable은 ‘치료할 수 없는, 불치의’라는 뜻으로, “previously incurable diseases”라는 본문 표현에서 질병을 치료할 수 없다는 의미로 올바르게 사용되었다. 반면 나머지 영영 풀이는 실제 의미와 다르다. ① demonstrate는 ‘보여 주다, 입증하다’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이에서는 ‘숨기다’라고 설명하여 틀렸다. ③ ethical은 ‘윤리적인, 도덕적으로 옳은’이라는 의미인데, 해로운 행동을 뜻한다고 설명하여 부적절하다. ④ comprehensive는 ‘포괄적인, 종합적인’이라는 뜻인데, ‘짧고 중요한 세부 사항이 부족한’이라고 설명해 틀렸다. ⑤ innovative는 ‘혁신적인, 새로운 아이디어를 도입하는’ 이라는 의미인데, ‘구식의’라고 설명하여 반대 의미가 되었다.

solution: ⓑ apply → applying (또는 To apply) 접속사 While이 이끄는 절 안에서 동사 raises(야기한다)의 주어 역할을 해야 하는 자리이다. 동사원형 apply는 문장의 주어가 될 수 없으므로 동명사 applying이나 to부정사인 To apply로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ ensuring → to ensure 문장 앞의 It은 가주어이며, ⓓ 이하 문장이 진주어 역할을 해야 한다. 가주어-진주어 구문에서 진주어로 쓰일 때 일반적으로 to부정사가 오므로 to ensure로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 상태/감각 동사 seem 뒤에서 주어를 설명하는 보어 자리로, promising이 '유망한/기대를 품게 하는'이라는 의미의 형용사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 동사 continue는 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취할 수 있으므로 to improve는 어법상 올바르다. ⓔ 접속사 while 뒤에 '주어+be동사(it is)'가 생략된 접속사를 남겨둔 분사구문이다. 능동의 의미로 목적어(the risk...)를 취하고 있으므로 현재분사 reducing이 올바르다.

One day, a fourteen-year-old girl named Josie visited the shop with her mother, Chrissie. Josie chatted with Klara joyfully. Josie immediately took a liking to Klara and asked whether Klara (A) (wanted / wanting) to be her friend.
Josie: I really want you to come to my home. I think you’ll like my room, and we’ll see the beautiful sunset from the windows there. We can do all the great things together all the time while I’m growing up. You want to come, right?
Klara: (nodding hopefully)
Josie: That’s so good, but I want to be honest with you. I know how bad you’ll feel after people promise you perfect things and they turn out not to (B) (be / being) so. Some days I’m not so healthy or happy. I do not know why. Do you still want to come, Klara?
Klara: If there’s anything difficult or scary, we will face it together. To show that she would do her best to be Josie’s friend, Klara held her hands together and shook them slightly. Pleased by Klara’s gesture of friendship, Josie asked Chrissie for her permission to buy the AF. Chrissie asked Klara what she had observed about Josie, and found Klara (C) (being / to be) highly observant. After requesting that Klara continue to care about Josie, Chrissie agreed to buy Klara and took her home.

But I don't think it would have worked out so well. After several rainy days, the Sun came out to shine light on Josie and her whole bed. Josie woke up and made a miraculous recovery. Seasons and years went by, and she grew into a healthy adult. When Josie left for college, Klara was sent to the Yard, a place where old AFs spend their remaining days at the end of their lives. In the Yard, she remembered her days with Josie.

ⓓ ) Mr. Capaldi believed there was nothing special inside Josie, but I believe now that there was something very special. But it wasn't inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. ( ⓔ ) I would have never reached what they felt for Josie in their hearts. I am sure of this now.
solution: 주어진 문장 'But I don't think it would have worked out so well.'은 역접 담화 표지 'But'으로 시작하여 앞에서 제시된 어떤 가능성에 대해 부정적인 평가를 내리는 내용이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 Klara가 Josie를 '계속할 수 있었다'는 가능성이 제시되어야 하고, 이 문장 뒤에는 그것이 잘 되지 않았을 이유에 대한 설명이 이어져야 한다. ⓒ 앞 문장은 'If it had become necessary, I could have continued Josie.'로, Klara가 Josie를 대신할 수 있었다는 가능성을 언급하고 있으며, ⓒ 뒤 문장은 'Not because I wouldn't have achieved accuracy, but however hard I tried, I believe now there would have remained something beyond my reach.'로 잘 되지 않았을 이유를 설명하고 있다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 ⓒ 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.

→
answer: ⓒ could continued → could have continued, ⓓ however hardly → however hard
solution: ⓒ could continued → could have continued 조건절 If it had become necessary(had p.p.)와 호응하는 가정법 과거완료 구문이다. 과거 사실에 대한 반대 상황을 표현해야 하므로 주절의 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형이 아닌 have p.p.가 와서 could have continued가 되어야 한다. ⓓ however hardly → however hard '아무리 ~할지라도'라는 양보의 부사절을 이끄는 복합관계부사 구문(however + 형용사/부사 + 주어 + 동사) 이다. 동사 tried(노력하다)를 수식하여 '아무리 열심히 노력했을지라도'라는 의미를 만들어야 하므로 부사 hard가 와야 한다. hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 부정을 나타내므로 문맥과 어법에 맞지 않다. ⓐ 장소 선행사 a place 뒤에 'old AFs(주어) + spend(동사) + their remaining days(목적어)'의 완전한 절이 연결되므로 관계부사 where가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓑ 선행사를 포함하여 do의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 관계대명사인 what이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 선행사를 포함하여 reached의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 관계대명사인 what이 올바르게 쓰였다.

In Josie's country home, Klara found out that Josie had gone through a procedure known as "lifting." By being lifted, Josie's cognitive abilities had been genetically enhanced so that she had a better chance of getting into prestigious universities. However, Josie was suffering from serious side effects similar to those that had claimed the life of her sister, Sal. A mysterious chronic illness often caused her to stay in bed for days on end. Because of this, Josie spent most of her time at home and was being educated there. One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi's studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after completing the questionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi's office. To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie suspended in the air—it was an AF replica of Josie's body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara's consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to die.

Why did Josie's lifting procedure result in such serious side effects?

What did Mr. Capaldi and Chrissie plan to do if the real Josie were to die?

choices: companion : a person or thing that spends time with or helps another
nourishment : a feeling of deep sadness and disappointment

solution: ① companion은 ‘함께 시간을 보내는 친구, 동반자’라는 뜻으로, 제시된 영영 풀이인 “a person or thing that spends time with or helps another”가 올바른 설명이다. 본문에서도 Klara는 아이들의 친구 역할을 하는 companion robot으로 소개된다. ② nourishment는 ‘영양, 자양분’이라는 뜻인데, 제시문에서는 “깊은 슬픔과 실망의 감정”이라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. ③ observe는 ‘관찰하다’라는 의미인데, 제시문은 “주변에서 일어나는 일을 완전히 무시하다”라고 설명하고 있어 틀렸다. ④ stroke는 ‘부드럽게 쓰다듬다’라는 뜻인데, 제시문에서는 “거칠고 폭력적으로 밀치거나 때리다”라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다. ⑤ restore는 ‘회복시키다, 원래 상태로 되돌리다’라는 의미인데, 제시문은 “영구적으로 파괴하거나 완전히 제거하다”라고 설명하고 있으므로 틀렸다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것의 개수는?
Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, ⓐintroduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem ⓑpromising, applying this technology to unborn babies ⓒraise ethical and social problems. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially
ⓓaffected an individual’s future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy. In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to ⓔhandle the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important ⓕto ensure that gene editing’s potential is employed for the greater good while
ⓖreducing the risk of unexpected results.
solution: ⓒ raise → raises While절 안에서 주어는 동명사구인 applying this technology to unborn babies이다. 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하므로 단수 동사 raises로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ affected → affecting 주절(CRISPR can introduce errors during editing) 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문이다. '개인의 미래 건강에 영향을 미치면서'라는 능동의 의미를 나타내고 뒤에 목적어(an individual's future health)가 오므로 현재분사 affecting으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ handle → handling be crucial to 구문에서 to는 부정사가 아닌 전치사이다. 따라서 뒤에 동사원형이 아닌 동명사 handling이 올바른 형태이다. ⓐ 주어인 The CRISPR gene-editing tool을 수식하는 과거분사로, '2012년에 소개된/도입된 도구'라는 수동의 의미이므로 introduced가 올바르다. ⓑ 감각/상태 동사 seem 뒤에서 보어 역할을 하는 형용사 (유망한, 기대를 갖게 하는)로 promising이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓕ 가주어 It에 대응하는 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사 구문으로 to ensure가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓖ 접속사 while 뒤에 주어+be동사(it is)가 생략된 접속사를 남겨둔 분사구문 형태이다. 능동의 의미로 목적어(the risk...) 를 취하고 있으므로 현재분사 reducing이 올바르다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 필자의 태도로 가장 적절한 것은?
Imagine a child who can speak more than ten languages or a child who demonstrates surprising mathematical skills. These unusually talented children may seem like something out of a science-fiction novel, but gene-editing technology has the potential to transform such fiction into reality. The CRISPR gene-editing tool, introduced in 2012, was developed to cure previously incurable diseases by targeting and modifying specific genes. While this may seem promising, applying this technology to unborn babies raises ethical and social problems. For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially affecting an individual's future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy. In conclusion, while CRISPR offers potential benefits, we must use it carefully and ethically. Responsible research and comprehensive guidelines are crucial to handling the ethical issues surrounding this innovative technology. It is important to ensure that gene editing's potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.
solution: ④ 필자는 글의 전반부에서 CRISPR 기술이 10개 이상의 언어를 구사하는 아이나 뛰어난 수학 능력을 가진 아이를 현실로 만들 잠재력이 있다고 소개하며, 기술의 가능성에 대해 열의 있는(enthusiastic) 태도를 보인다. 그러나 후반부에서는 기술 사용에 신중해야 함을 강조하는 조심스러운(cautious) 태도로 전환된다. 따라서 enthusiastic(열의 있는) → cautious(신중한)가 정답이다. ① optimistic(낙관적인) → indifferent(무관심한) ② impressed(감명받은) → alarmed(불안해하는) ③ curious(호기심 있는) → relieved(안도하는) ⑤ confused(혼란스러운) → confident(자신감 있는)

For example, the birth of customized babies could intensify social unfairness if these techniques are only accessible to rich individuals or countries. Moreover, CRISPR can introduce errors during editing, potentially affecting an individual's future health. Though technology may continue to improve, it has not yet achieved error-free accuracy.

It is important to ensure that gene editing's potential is employed for the greater good while reducing the risk of unexpected results.
보기 raise / technology / this / ethical / social / problems / and / to / unborn babies / apply
조건 1. 보기의 단어들만 모두 사용하되, 필요시 단어 의 형태를 변형할 것
2. 동명사를 주어로 사용할 것
→
answer: applying this technology to unborn babies raises ethical and social problems
solution: 이 문장은 '이 기술을 적용하는 것은(주어) + 태아에게 (수식어구) + 야기한다(동사) + 윤리적·사회적 문제들을 (목적어)'의 구조로 써야 한다. 우선 '이 기술을 적용하는 것'이라는 주어를 만들기 위해 동사 apply를 동명사 applying으로 바꾸고, 적용 대상을 뜻하는 to unborn babies를 붙여 applying this technology to unborn babies라는 동명사 주어구를 만든다. 이어서 '야기한다'에 해당하는 동사를 배치할 때, 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하므로 바로 앞의 복수 명사(unborn babies)에 유의하여 raise를 단수 동사 raises로 형태를 변형해야 한다. 마지막으로 동사의 목적어로 '윤리적이고 사회적인 문제들'을 뜻하는 ethical and social problems를 차례대로 연결하여 전체 문장을 올바르게 완성한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
One day when Josie felt better, her mother took her and Klara to the city so that Josie could have her portrait done by Mr. Capaldi. In Capaldi's studio, Klara was asked to answer a questionnaire about Josie. Looking around the studio after completing the ⓐquestionnaire, Klara entered Capaldi's office. To her surprise, she saw something that looked like Josie ⓑsuspended in the air - it was an AF replica of Josie's body! As it turned out, Mr. Capaldi was not a painter but a scientist, who planned with Chrissie to transfer Klara's consciousness to the replica and make a new Josie if the real Josie were to die.
Capaldi: Klara, (A)
Klara: It resembles Josie quite accurately. Mr. Capaldi, you have done a good job of ⓒcapturing Josie's appearance. I now understand why Chrissie asked me, at every step, to observe and learn Josie. The survey seems to test how well I have come to know Josie and how well I understand her decisions and feelings.
Capaldi: We will ask you to become her and to live in that replica of Josie with everything you have learned. Learn Josie, not just ⓓsuperficially, but deeply, entirely. You have to continue her for Chrissie and for everyone else who loves Josie.
Chrissie: (B) _____ I'm still not sure if this whole plan is the best thing we can do. I have been afraid of losing Josie ever since I lost Sal. That is why I agreed with you on this replica, but however well you make it, I don't think I will be able to accept this AF as my Josie.
Capaldi: You must not lose faith, Chrissie. The survey Klara has successfully completed is clear evidence that she is already well on her way to understanding all of Josie's drives and desires. You believe that there is something unreachable inside each of us, something that is unique and won't transfer. But there is nothing like that. The new Josie won't be an imitation. She will be the exact same person and you will have every right to love her just as you love Josie now.
Chrissie: But will I believe in it? When the day comes, will I really?
Klara: Excuse me, but I would like to say there is a chance you will never need the new Josie. She may ⓔovercome her illness. If the day comes when you do need the new Josie, I will do my best to become as close to her as possible. However, it is wrong to give up hope already.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영 풀이 의미가 문맥상 어색한것은?
choices: ⓐquestionnaire: a written set of questions that are given to people in order to collect facts or opinions about something
ⓑsuspend: to hang something so that it is free on all sides except at the point of support
ⓒcapture: to take into one's possession or control by force
ⓓsuperficially: as to the outward appearance only; on the surface
ⓔovercome: to successfully deal with or gain control of (something difficult)
solution: ③ capture(정확히 포착하다)는 '무력으로 소유하거나 통제하다'의 의미로 문맥상 어색하다.
